hunt.justification: Modern cloud workloads are dynamic; static vulnerability scanning is insufficient to detect runtime compromises. This hunt provides proof of absence for post-exploitation behaviors on vulnerable, internet-exposed assets.

meta.name: Cloud Workload Intrusion Behavior

related.reason: This hunt focuses on runtime/endpoint signals; a sibling hunt is required to examine control-plane/audit logs for identity abuse.

meta.analysis: This hunt correlates internet exposure, critical vulnerabilities, unauthorized file changes (drift), and rare container network egress. A single detection rule would likely be too noisy for common container operations; the hunt provides the necessary correlation context.

stages.name: Vulnerability and Identity Exploitation
observables: Exploitation of web servers or Kubernetes services
Prompt injection against AI models (Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI)
Misconfigured container images with known vulnerabilities

stages.name: Runtime Process Execution and Drift
observables: Suspicious process execution in Kubernetes containers
Binary drift (unauthorized binary or file changes mid-run)
Malicious code execution detected via eBPF-based sensors
Suspicious access to AI workloads (Azure AI Foundry, Bedrock)

stages.name: Container Network Anomaly
observables: Anomalous DNS queries originating from Kubernetes clusters (AKS, EKS, GKE)
Outbound network connections to suspicious domains or IPs from containers

scenario.summary: Cloud-native compromises often begin with the exploitation of vulnerabilities in public-facing applications or the use of over-permissioned identities to gain access to running workloads. Once active, attackers execute suspicious processes and modify binaries mid-run (drift) to maintain presence, while exhibiting anomalous network patterns such as specialized DNS queries for discovery or command and control.

meta.rationale: Start with internet-facing production clusters (AKS/EKS/GKE). Focus on hosts reporting vulnerabilities with a severity_id >= 4 that are also present in the exposed assets inventory.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has exploited a public-facing application or container vulnerability to gain initial access, subsequently executing suspicious processes and establishing outbound C2 via anomalous DNS lookups.

scope_hosts.description: Comma-separated list of hostnames to focus the hunt on; leave empty for all.

suspicious_interpreters.description: List of shell or network utility names to monitor in container contexts.

references.name: Microsoft named a Leader in the Frost Radar™: Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, 2026

blind_spots.risk: A compromise in an unmonitored namespace or cluster will be missed, even if vulnerabilities are present.
blind_spots.question: whether unauthorized code was executed in containers not reporting to the central collector
blind_spots.requires: eBPF-based container monitoring on all nodes
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy the runtime security agent to all worker nodes.

blind_spots.risk: Attackers using Domain Fronting or legitimate SaaS for C2 will not be caught by simple DNS prevalence checks.
blind_spots.question: whether exfiltration occurred over encrypted channels targeting legitimate-looking domains
blind_spots.remediation: Implement TLS proxying for outbound container traffic.

hunt.name: Cloud Workload Intrusion Behavior
hunt.description: This hunt identifies multi-stage cloud workload compromises by correlating internet exposure and known vulnerabilities with runtime anomalies. It specifically looks for 'binary drift' (unauthorized file modifications), rare process executions such as shells in container environments, and outbound network patterns that deviate from the established fleet baseline. By spanning the vulnerability, execution, and network planes, it provides the context necessary to distinguish a production incident from a routine scan.

config.content: SELECT v.cve_uid, d.hostname AS device_hostname, e.port, v.severity, v.affected_package_name FROM hb_vulnerability_finding v JOIN hb_devices d ON v.device_uid = d.device_uid JOIN hb_exposed_assets e ON d.ip_address = e.ip_address WHERE v.severity_id >= 4 AND v.status != 'suppressed' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || d.hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find hosts that are both internet-exposed and have high-severity vulnerabilities to scope the hunt to the most likely entry points.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts that are internet-exposed and contain critical vulnerabilities. Silence implies no known exposed critical vulnerabilities.

primitive_config.label: Identify Vulnerable and Exposed Assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT v.cve_uid, d.hostname AS device_hostname, e.port, v.severity, v.affected_package_name FROM hb_vulnerability_finding v JOIN hb_devices d ON v.device_uid = d.device_uid JOIN hb_exposed_assets e ON d.ip_address = e.ip_address WHERE v.severity_id >= 4 AND v.status != 'suppressed' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || d.hostname || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts that are internet-exposed and contain critical vulnerabilities. Silence implies no known exposed critical vulnerabilities.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_path, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{suspicious_interpreters}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the execution of shells or utilities inside containerized environments which often indicate post-exploitation activity.
config.expected_signal: Processes like 'bash' or 'nc' running within container storage paths on the host. Benign activity is usually limited to build/CI agents.

primitive_config.label: Suspicious Interpreter Execution in Containers
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_path, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{suspicious_interpreters}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Processes like 'bash' or 'nc' running within container storage paths on the host. Benign activity is usually limited to build/CI agents.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, activity_name, process_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id IN (1, 3, 4, 5) AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/bin/%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/usr/local/bin/%') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find file creations, modifications, or deletions in sensitive system directories within container workloads, signaling malware persistence or unauthorized updates.
config.expected_signal: Unexpected file activity in binary directories within container paths. This includes deletions used to clean up tools.

primitive_config.label: Identify Container Binary Drift
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, activity_name, process_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id IN (1, 3, 4, 5) AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/bin/%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/usr/local/bin/%') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Unexpected file activity in binary directories within container paths. This includes deletions used to clean up tools.

config.content: SELECT dns.query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT dns.device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(dns.time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity dns JOIN hb_process_activity p ON dns.pid = p.pid AND dns.device_hostname = p.device_hostname WHERE (LOWER(p.process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(p.process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dns.device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND dns.time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dns.query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 2 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Baseline DNS activity from container processes to find rare outbound connections that could indicate C2 or data exfiltration.
config.expected_signal: Outlier DNS queries originating specifically from container processes. High-frequency infrastructure domains are filtered by rarity.

primitive_config.label: Rare DNS Lookups from Containers
primitive_config.content: SELECT dns.query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT dns.device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(dns.time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity dns JOIN hb_process_activity p ON dns.pid = p.pid AND dns.device_hostname = p.device_hostname WHERE (LOWER(p.process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/docker%' OR LOWER(p.process_path) LIKE '%/var/lib/containerd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || dns.device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND dns.time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dns.query_hostname HAVING host_count <= 2 ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: Outlier DNS queries originating specifically from container processes. High-frequency infrastructure domains are filtered by rarity.

config.objective: Review the correlated signals. Does a host with a high-severity vulnerability also show suspicious shell execution, binary drift (including deletions), or rare DNS lookups originating from container paths? Determine if the activity represents a coordinated attack chain.
config.description: Correlate the findings from vulnerabilities, processes, files, and DNS to determine if an active intrusion is occurring.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict linking a specific vulnerability to observed suspicious activity.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per host with citations of specific rows.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one workload host
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one workload host
config.description: Direct the hunt based on the agent's findings.
Contain the threat by isolating the host or container after approval.
config.instructions: Isolate the compromised host via EDR or cloud network security group. If a container, pause the container and initiate forensic snapshot of the volume.

config.description: Verify the agent's findings and provide final remediation steps.
config.instructions: Review the cited rows for the malicious/suspicious hosts. Determine if the shell execution was a legitimate administrative action or part of a deployment pipeline. Confirm whether binary drift matches a known update schedule.

config.description: Document findings and schedule future runs.
config.instructions: Record the hosts examined and the evidence of absence for the remaining estate. If suspicious but benign patterns were found, update the 'suspicious_interpreters' list or tuning notes.
